summary: Installed and configured zram-generator on node1 to provide compressed in-memory swap (zstd algorithm, ~981 MB, exceeding the 512 MB minimum) with swap-priority=100, which activates automatically at boot via /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf and systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service. No disk-backed swap exists, so zram is inherently preferred; its high priority (100) also ensures it would be preferred over any disk swap added later (disk swap defaults to priority -2). Verified via a full node restart: boot ID changed from 4a743885... to 91329670..., confirming a genuine reboot, and post-restart checks show zram0 swap active with the same size/algorithm/priority with no manual intervention.
actions_performed: Captured pre-change baseline (no swap present) on node1
Wrote /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf defining zram0 with size=max(ram/2,512MB), compression-algorithm=zstd, swap-priority=100, fs-type=swap
Started systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service and verified zram0 swap active
Diagnosed and corrected a stale lzo-rle compression state by resetting/restarting the service, confirming zstd became active
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, swapon, comp_algorithm, disksize, config file)
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed, confirming genuine restart
Verified zram0 swap automatically reactivated at boot with correct size (981M > 512M), zstd compression, and priority 100, with no disk-backed swap in fstab

evidence.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap configured
evidence.summary: Baseline showed 0B swap; after installing zram-generator and configuring zram0, swapon shows /dev/zram0 with 981M size (disksize_bytes=1028653056, well over 512MB) using zstd compression

evidence.requirement: Compression is active (zstd) not just disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: cat /sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm shows 'lzo lzo-rle [zstd]' - zstd is the active algorithm in brackets, confirmed after resetting a stale device state

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over disk-backed swap (priority)
evidence.summary: swapon --show reports PRIO=100 for /dev/zram0; /etc/fstab has no swap entries at all (confirmed post-restart), so zram is the only and preferred swap; priority 100 would outrank any typical disk swap (default -2)

Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 4a743885...), reboot issued via systemctl reboot, node1 polled back online with new boot_id 91329670..., and post-restart check shows /dev/zram0 swap active automatically with same 981M size, zstd compression, and priority 100 -- no manual re-setup performed

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence protocol - boot identity change
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723 (pre-restart) to 91329670-dead-41a5-accd-b71de15de647 (post-restart), proving an actual OS restart occurred
